Updated: 22 October 2026

For information on data fields, please see the police recorded crime and outcomes open data user guide. Available from:

Amendments to outcome headings: 
The heading have been changed to give users greater clarity on these columns. 'Force outcomes for offences recorded in quarter' has been renamed to 'Outcomes for offences that were recorded in the quarter' and  'Force outcomes recorded in quarter' has been renamed to' Outcomes for investigations closed in the quarter'.

Amendments to subgroups:

Users should note that the subgroups have been changed to align with those used by ONS in their quarterly Crime in England and Wales statistical outputs. This includes creating a new subgroup of vehicle offences which is the sum of the previously published subgroups of: theft from a vehicle, theft of a motor vehicle, aggravated vehicle taking and vehicle interference (offence codes 45, 48, 37.2, 126).

Furthermore, from April 2023 we added the subgroups of residential burglary and non-residential burglary which brings these into line with a new classification of burglary offences which was introduced from April 2017. These new sub-groups have replaced domestic and non-domestic burglary respectively. Between April 2017 and March 2023 residential burglary included burglary (including attempts) of all buildings or parts of buildings that are within the boundary of, or form a part of, a dwelling. Users should note that, from April 2023, further sub-categories of residential burglary were introduced to separate out burglaries from the main dwelling (residential - home) and other unconnected buildings (residential - unconnected buildings). Burglary offence codes 28E, 28F, 28G, 28H and 29A have been replaced by offence codes 28I, 28J, 28K, 28L, 28M, 28N, 28O, 28P 29B and 29C.
New outcome codes were introduced on 1st April 2026  'Child Deferred Prosecution' and 'Adult Deferred Prosecution'.
Force Notes

British Transport Police - due to IT difficulties Outcome 22 are not showing when there has been finalised crimes under Outcome 22. The force will endeavour to get this resolved as soon as possible.  From April 2024, data may not represent the same figures captured locally for the force.

It is important to note that data from the police can be influenced by improvements and changes to recording processes and practices by the police. Data can also be affected by changes to administrative processes, such as prioritisation being given to other tasks which may lead to backlogs which when cleared can skew distributions.
Additional Notes

The Ministry of Justice has been working with the Home Office, the Crown Prosecution Service and the National Police Chiefs’ Council to make the use of out-of-court disposals for adult offenders more effective. 

In November 2014, as part of this project, three police forces (Leicestershire, Staffordshire and West Yorkshire) started a 12 month pilot of simplified outcomes. All three forces stopped issuing adult simple cautions (part of outcome 3) and cannabis / khat warnings (outcome 7) and limited their use of penalty notices for disorder (outcome 6). They used the adult conditional caution (part of outcome 3) and the community resolution (outcome 8) instead. These three pilot forces have continued to use the simplified outcomes since the pilot ended in November 2015. So Leicestershire, Staffordshire and West Yorkshire will have a smaller proportion of outcomes 6 and 7 and a greater proportion of outcome 8 than other forces. Since this pilot, some other forces have also limited their use of some out of court disposals. This may lead to apparent falls in some of these outcome types (e.g. cannabis/khat warnings) which may be accompanied by increases in outcomes 3 and 8 which will have been used in their place.

To provide more transparency, new outcome sub-categories were introduced from April 2016 to give additional detail on where an alternative offence has been charged/cautioned to the one that was recorded. These alternative outcomes were created as the following sub-categories: charge/summons (outcome 1A), youth caution (outcome 2A) and adult caution (outcome 3A) and in this dataset are included within outcomes 1, 2 and 3 accordingly. For a breakdown of these offences please see Outcomes for Alternate Offences Open Data Tables from Year ending March 2017 available at:
https://www.gov.uk/government/statistical-data-sets/police-recorded-crime-and-outcomes-open-data-tables

or write to:  Home Office Crime Analysis Unit, 5th Floor, 2 Ruskin Square, Dingwall Road, Croydon CR0 2WF

Amendments to subgroups:

Users should note that the subgroups have been changed to align with those used by ONS in their quarterly Crime in England and Wales statistical outputs. This includes creating a new subgroup of vehicle offences which is the sum of the previously published subgroups of: theft from a vehicle, theft of a motor vehicle, aggravated vehicle taking and vehicle interference (offence codes 45, 48, 37.2, 126).

These three pilot forces have continued to use the simplified outcomes since the pilot ended in November 2015. So Leicestershire, Staffordshire and West Yorkshire will have a smaller proportion of outcomes 6 and 7 and a greater proportion of outcome 8 than other forces.
